key_insight: Instead of reusing the same text or class embedding at every diffusion step, this paper proposes predicting the next embedding in sequence and using it as the condition. This makes image generation more dynamic by letting the model evolve its guidance over denoising steps.
problem_solved: Diffusion transformers typically rely on a fixed condition embedding throughout generation, which may limit expressiveness and adaptability. The paper explores whether predicted continuous embeddings can better guide image generation than a static prompt or class label.
method: Introduce Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA), a Transformer trained to predict the next continuous embedding in a sequence.
During generation, treat the clean image embedding as the next embedding after the condition and noisy-image embeddings.
Use predicted embeddings as evolving conditioning signals across denoising steps instead of a single reused embedding.
impact: This approach could improve diffusion-based image generation by making conditioning more adaptive and context-aware. For practitioners, it suggests a new way to design generative models that better align conditioning with the progression of the denoising process.
